intro: The last Asian-looking painting on the homepage. Two California mornings to take its place, each laid on the real homepage. Only the painting changes; the words stay. On a laptop the painting also runs off the screen's edge a little less, so nothing in it is cut in half.

looks.name: Breakfast on the back porch
looks.what: Coffee, orange juice, a bowl of oranges, poppies in a jam jar, a brown paper lunch bag and the car keys, on a porch looking out at golden hills and a valley oak. A busy family morning, plainly in California.
looks.note: California at one look, and the oak fills the corner the blossom used to. Holding it back: it is softer watercolour than the Big Sur painting at the bottom of the page.
rest: Michael, “I read up on it first”: the same porch at dusk, an open book and reading glasses on the arm of a wooden porch chair, a mug beside it.
Susan, “The source mattered to me”: on the porch table, a piece of honeycomb on a board beside a sprig of the green Brazilian shrub the bees take their resin from.

looks.name: The kitchen table by the window
looks.what: The same breakfast things on the kitchen table, with the backyard lemon tree in the window behind.
looks.note: Warm and homey. But a kitchen could be anywhere; only the lemons say California, and the window frame is faint.
rest: Michael: the same table in the evening, an open book, reading glasses and a mug, the lemon tree dark in the window.
Susan: on the table, a piece of honeycomb on a board beside a sprig of the green Brazilian shrub.
